disclosure.bar: Fictional restaurant — a concept design by Simplified Tech Solutions. Menu, prices, address and hours are samples.
disclosure.footer: Jade & Ember is a fictional restaurant created by Simplified Tech Solutions as a website design concept. It does not exist. All menu items, prices, the address, the phone number and the opening hours are invented samples. Food imagery and the hero video are AI-generated concept media and do not depict real dishes served by any restaurant.

headline: The breath
of the wok.
hero.text: Carbon steel, a flame at full height, and a kitchen that cooks to the second. Tuesday to Sunday, from five.
hero.caption: Wok-seared beef, broccoli, red chili

image.alt: A carbon steel wok on a roaring burner: sliced beef, broccoli and red chili in the pan under a tall flare of orange flame, with steam rising into a dark kitchen.

intro.label: Wok hei
intro.body: Wok hei, the breath of the wok, is the smoky, singed sweetness that only comes from food moving fast over a very hot flame. Four things make it, and we cook around all of them.

items.name: Fire
items.text: A burner kept at full height, so the pan never has time to cool.

items.name: Steam
items.text: Wine and stock flash at the wall of the wok and lift the aroma into the dish.

items.name: Texture
items.text: Small cuts, dry ingredients, and a toss that never stops. Crisp stays crisp.

items.name: The plate
items.text: Out of the wok and onto jade or slate within seconds, while it is still singing.

signature.label: Signature

items.alt: Mapo tofu in a jade-green celadon bowl: silken tofu in red chili oil with minced beef, Sichuan peppercorns and scallion, steam rising, on a slate board.

items.name: Char Siu

story.label: Story
story.pull: A small kitchen, one very hot wok.
paragraphs: Jade & Ember began as a question about a single flame: what if a dining room felt like standing beside a wok at full heat, without the noise or the smoke?

The room is charcoal and slate, lit low, with celadon bowls stacked on the pass. The kitchen cooks Cantonese and Sichuan dishes with a lighter hand, and the menu stays short so every dish gets its turn at the fire.
Jade for the bowls, ember for the flame. The name is the whole palette.
story.caption: Celadon rice bowls, stacked on the pass.
